name: SCiEL: Moving sofa spatial grid proxy
description: Choose a three-dimensional rigid motion path through the specified corridor to maximize feasible voxel volume on a grid of spacing 0.05.

moving_sofa_3d_path.docstring:
The 3D moving sofa problem: find the largest-volume rigid 3D shape that can
travel through an L-shaped 3D corridor of unit cross-section that has two
90-degree turns - one in the X-Y plane and one in the Y-Z plane (a 3D
generalisation of the classical 2D moving sofa problem).

The shape itself is recovered (in the evaluator) by sweeping a solid block
along a motion path and keeping every sub-volume that stays inside the
corridor for the whole path. The "solution" we evolve is therefore that
motion path: a sequence of rigid-body poses for the block.

A pose is a 6-tuple (x, y, z, yaw, pitch, roll), where (yaw, pitch, roll)
are extrinsic Euler angles in DEGREES (applied about the fixed z, y, x axes,
i.e. R = Rx(roll) @ Ry(pitch) @ Rz(yaw)) and (x, y, z) is a translation. To
place the block in a pose we first rotate it about the origin, then
translate it. The evaluator prepends a fixed start pose and appends a fixed
end pose, then densifies (smooths) the path before sweeping the block.

This baseline path is exactly the construction AlphaEvolve reported for this
problem in "Mathematical Discovery and Exploration at Scale" (2025), which
achieves a swept volume of about 1.81 at fine grid resolution.

Returns:
    path: np.ndarray of shape (99, 6), each row a pose
        (x, y, z, yaw_deg, pitch_deg, roll_deg).

upstream_contract.validity_semantics: No independent boolean validity field; zero score, success rate and absence of error do not establish validity.
upstream_contract.error_semantics: Original return branches are retained verbatim as source expressions. Some branches return score zero without error; some omit the primary score. Missing primary scores, exceptions, timeout and nonfinite JSON fail in the common adapter. An absent error field does not imply validity.

budgets.enforcement: These are original search/config budgets. Direct evaluation uses callable defaults and the common runner outer timeout; config max_iterations does not run a search.
